page: Microsoft Azure E16s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock of 2.8 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound computational tasks. In memory throughput testing, the server achieves 690.78 GB/sec on cached read-only 16 KB blocks, alongside uncached 256 MB transfer rates of 96.64 GB/sec for reads and 55.64 GB/sec for writes. The instance does not include dedicated GPUs or local instance storage, requiring remote Premium Storage disks for persistent file system operations and secondary caching layers.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-core and memory-heavy tests, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 15,546.06, a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,567.0, and 12.92 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-thread compute capabilities remain modest, registering weak scores on stress-ng single-core tests (1,412.98) and bzip3 single-threaded decompression (8.63 GB/sec). Prompt processing on medium 7B parameter language models also benchmarks in the bottom quartile at 24.19 tokens per second.

The hardware profile delivers solid cost efficiency when utilized for memory-density applications rather than intensive single-threaded execution. Microsoft Azure E16s_v4 is well aligned for enterprise relational databases, in-memory key-value caches like Redis, mid-sized data processing pipelines, and general memory-heavy analytical tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E16s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system RAM, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU distribution. Built on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor at 2.8 GHz across 8 physical cores, the platform incorporates AVX-512 vector extensions and 48 MB of L3 cache. It contains no onboard GPUs and has no local ephemeral storage, depending entirely on networked Premium Storage options. Synthetic benchmarks indicate average multi-threaded execution and steady memory bandwidth, highlighted by 12.92 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark CPU score of 15,546.06, and 96.64 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Conversely, single-threaded processing reflects lower relative performance. This instance serves workloads requiring sizable memory density, including relational databases, in-memory caching layers, and multi-threaded enterprise processing.
